mxc_help.output:
Linux Container Executor

Usage: lxc-exec [OPTIONS] [CONFIG_PATH]

Arguments:
  [CONFIG_PATH]  Path to config JSON file (positional)

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>                Path to config JSON file
      --config-base64 <CONFIG_BASE64>  Base64-encoded JSON config
      --debug                          Enable debug/console output
      --delete                         Delete container mode
      --containername <CONTAINERNAME>  Container name (required with --delete)
      --experimental                   Enable experimental features
      --allow-testing-features         Allow testing-only features that must never run in production, currently `network.proxy.builtinTestServer` (a bundled, deliberately-permissive test HTTP proxy). Distinct from --experimental
      --available-backends             Report host backend availability as JSON and exit
      --dry-run                        Parse and validate config then exit without executing
      --log-file <LOG_FILE>            Path to diagnostic log file (appends, creates if missing)
      --setup-hyperlight[=<RUNTIMES>]  Install the warmed Hyperlight snapshot and exit, for the default runtime (`agent`) or the comma-separated runtimes given with `=`: `--setup-hyperlight=python,node`. Names are `agent`, `python`, `python-shell`, `node`, `bash` and `dotnet-jit`. For each, pulls the published rootfs from GHCR unless the image home already holds it, boots it once, and writes the snapshot into the default user data dir (~/.local/share/mxc-hyperlight on Linux, %LOCALAPPDATA%\mxc-hyperlight on Windows). $MXC_HYPERLIGHT_HOME overrides the destination if set. Intended for tool install hooks so first-run has zero warmup cost
      --force                          Rebuild the snapshot even if one already exists. Use after replacing `initrd.cpio` so the warm state matches the new bits. Requires --setup-hyperlight
  -h, --help                           Print help
